purpose: Verification of the hardened Level 8 load generator (summary schema level8-loadgen-summary/2). This is evidence about the MEASUREMENT SYSTEM, not an operational acceptance result for the service.
historical_evidence_status: unchanged and byte-identical; its operational acceptance result remains FAIL
historical_clarification: The original mixed_load.json success_over_scheduled value of 0.8807 refers to the measurement window, with 2,642 successful predictions out of 3,000 scheduled arrivals. The whole-run success rate is 3,642 out of 4,000, or 91.05%. The original field name was ambiguous, but the reported arithmetic was consistent. The original benchmark evidence remains unchanged and its operational acceptance result remains FAIL. The corrected harness uses a total client deadline rather than the historical per-phase-only timeout behavior. Future latency and failure distributions are therefore not directly interchangeable with historical measurements.

defects_found_in_the_committed_harness.defect: scheduled_in_window was derived from the scheduling-lag list, which only contains issued requests; scheduled arrivals were never counted independently
defects_found_in_the_committed_harness.correction: deterministic schedule (arrival k at t_start + k/rate), counted analytically and recorded per arrival in a ledger; scheduled = attempted + missed is an invariant

defects_found_in_the_committed_harness.defect: the in-flight count was incremented when a request task started running, so tasks created but not yet started were not bounded (observed in-flight 143 against a configured 100 and 128 connections)
defects_found_in_the_committed_harness.correction: capacity is reserved synchronously before the task is created, held until the task finishes (including waiting for a pooled connection), and released exactly once on every path

defects_found_in_the_committed_harness.defect: missed arrivals were a single counter without identity, time, cohort or reason
defects_found_in_the_committed_harness.correction: every missed arrival is a ledger record with identity, scheduled and detection times, cohort and a fixed reason code

defects_found_in_the_committed_harness.defect: the 2 s httpx timeout was a per-phase timeout; requests ran up to 7.8 s without a client timeout
defects_found_in_the_committed_harness.correction: one absolute total deadline per attempted request from task start, covering pool acquisition, connection, transmission, body, parsing and validation; late completions are client deadlines; httpx phase timeouts stay as subordinate safeguards

defects_found_in_the_committed_harness.defect: rates did not name their denominators and success_fraction used completed requests
defects_found_in_the_committed_harness.correction: every rate carries numerator, denominator and denominator_is; null for zero denominators; attempted-request and scheduled-arrival success rates are separate

defects_found_in_the_committed_harness.defect: no cohort-separated reconciliation, outstanding-at-end or drain duration
defects_found_in_the_committed_harness.correction: warm-up, measurement and whole-run blocks per stream with reconciliation invariants, outstanding work at measurement end, drain duration and completion-window throughput

contracts.arrival_schedule: arrival k is scheduled at t_start + k/rate on a monotonic clock; warm-up is the half-open interval [0, warmup), measurement is [warmup, warmup + measure); 100/s with 10 s + 30 s gives exactly 1,000 + 3,000 = 4,000 and 40/s gives 400 + 1,200 = 1,600; cohort follows the SCHEDULED time
contracts.late_arrival_policy: unchanged in substance and now explicit: a late arrival is issued as soon as the scheduler resumes, in schedule order; there is no lateness cutoff and no unbounded catch-up burst because every arrival must first reserve capacity; reasons for a miss: capacity_exhausted, task_creation_failed, cancelled_before_start, not_reached_before_stop; detection lag is recorded per miss
contracts.capacity: generator capacity per traffic kind (--max-backlog, default 100) is distinct from the HTTP connection-pool limit (--max-connections, default 128) and from the server's dispatcher capacity
contracts.total_deadline: --timeout (default 2 s) is the total client deadline measured from task start; phase timeouts are set to the same value as subordinate safeguards; synchronous JSON parsing and validation cannot be interrupted, so the deadline is checked after them; this is an application-level deadline, not a wall-clock guarantee under event-loop starvation; the production 500 ms admission and 250 ms execution deadlines are unchanged and unrelated
contracts.server_504: a 504 received before the deadline is an http_error with status 504, not a client deadline
contracts.closed_loop: no offered-arrival denominator is invented: scheduled counts and scheduled-arrival rates are null; attempted iterations, outcomes and throughput are reported
contracts.percentiles: linear interpolation between closest ranks; an empty sample gives n = 0 and null statistics; missed arrivals never contribute to any latency sample

denominator_definitions.success_rate_of_attempted: successful / attempted requests in the same cohort
denominator_definitions.success_rate_of_scheduled: successful / scheduled arrivals in the same cohort (open-loop and burst streams only)

test_methodology.deterministic: injectable clock, fake scheduler time (arrivals already due never yield), fake post functions, synthetic ledgers; no real-time sleeping is the primary mechanism for accounting, capacity or boundary tests; the hung-acquisition, multi-phase and slow-body deadline tests and the five socket tests use small real asyncio timers with large margins
test_methodology.socket_level: a controlled in-test HTTP/1.1 server on 127.0.0.1 with real asyncio sockets and httpx; no production endpoint and no Level 8 service involved
test_methodology.smoke: one short run of the hardened generator against the committed flat-image Level 8 service on an isolated Docker network; not an operational benchmark

full_level8_suite_repository_layout.note: the 3 skips are 2 opt-in engine tests and the flat-image module reporting NOT APPLICABLE in the repository layout

test_results.stability: After one timing-sensitive socket test was widened, the harness suite passed five consecutive runs: three standalone, one with four CPU-bound processes sharing the container, and one inside the full 217-test suite. Before that change the same test failed once in the full-suite run (a 0.25 s total deadline across 25 concurrent connections), which is recorded here.
test_results.historical_fixture: P2 repetition 3 arithmetic reproduced from synthetic records: whole run scheduled 4000, attempted 3642, successful 3642, missed 358, scheduled-arrival success 0.9105 (denominator 4000); measurement scheduled 3000, attempted 2642, successful 2642, missed 358, scheduled-arrival success 0.880667 (denominator 3000); the rates are separately labelled cohort blocks

socket_level_results: mixed outcomes over real sockets: 5 success, 10 http_error (503 and 504), 5 client_deadline, 5 transport_failure
total deadline enforced while phase timeouts were 5 s, and the server observed the client disconnect
pool contention: with a 2-connection pool the queued requests failed on the total deadline (pool wait counts)
open-loop at 200/s with capacity 5: max outstanding never above 5, capacity_exhausted misses recorded, scheduled = attempted + missed, no unterminated attempts
cancelling a run mid-flight: all reservations released once, no leaked tasks

smoke_against_the_committed_service.description: predict 50/s open-loop, explain 10/s open-loop, 2 closed-loop explain callers, burst of 8, 1 s warm-up + 4 s measurement, flat image, isolated network

success_rate_of_scheduled.denominator_is: not defined for closed-loop traffic (no offered arrivals)

smoke_against_the_committed_service.observation: the committed service's 503 explanation_overloaded responses (burst) were accepted as valid http_error outcomes with the correct Retry-After; capacity violations 0; the original request validation passed on every response

capacity_and_cancellation_observations.reservation_before_task_start: 500 due arrivals with capacity 10 created exactly 10 tasks and 490 recorded misses without a single task having started
capacity_and_cancellation_observations.release_exactly_once: double_release_attempts stayed 0 in every deterministic and socket test

unchanged: the 50 deterministic inputs, expected results, response validation and profile rates
intentionally_changed: --timeout is now the TOTAL client deadline (was httpx per-phase only)
--max-backlog is the generator capacity per traffic kind including reserved, waiting and executing work (was a count of started tasks)
the summary schema is new (level8-loadgen-summary/2: streams, cohorts, ledger-based counts); the raw file now holds one record per arrival or iteration including missed arrivals
invalid configurations (non-positive rates or durations, callers above capacity) are rejected with exit code 2
cli_and_schema_compatibility.historical_scripts: the scratch orchestrators used for L8-2D/L8-2DV read the old schema and are not compatible; the committed historical evidence is not reinterpreted

acceptance_gates.gate: scheduled arrivals counted independently of attempts
scheduled = attempted + missed for every finalized open-loop cohort
attempted = successful + failed after drain, outcomes mutually exclusive
no generator-capacity violations; reservation before task creation
every missed arrival represented with identity, times, cohort and reason
total deadline semantics (before, at, after; phases; acquisition; synchronous validation; 504 vs deadline)
no leaked tasks or reservations after drain or cancellation
warm-up and measurement cohorts reconcile independently
historical denominator arithmetic reproduced with unambiguous labelling
existing response validation and workload unchanged (fingerprint and profile table pinned)
no production file changed; historical evidence byte-identical

acceptance_gates.detail: by design an application-level deadline; not claimed

known_limitations: The total deadline is cooperative: it cannot interrupt synchronous parsing and validation and is not a wall-clock guarantee when the event loop is starved.
Socket-level tests use a controlled in-test server on loopback, not the Level 8 service; the Level 8 compatibility evidence is one short smoke run.
The deadline tests that use real timers and the five socket tests are the only timing-sensitive tests; they passed repeatedly, including under CPU saturation, but are not clock-independent.
Only the hardened generator is verified here; no operational benchmark was rerun, so no new service measurements exist and historical results are not reinterpreted.
The consumed-holdout uncertainty documented in mixed_load.json is unchanged.
